newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says it supports Malta's desire to join EU.
newsitem.headline: Italy says it supports Malta's desire to join EU.

text.p: Italy reaffirmed on Thursday that it would support efforts by Malta, its island neighbour in the southern Mediterranean, to join the European Union.

"I gave guarantees that Italy would give its full support to Malta regarding its application to join the European Union," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said after meeting Maltese Foreign Minister Guido De Marco.
De Marco said Malta wanted to join the EU not only for the economic benefits it would receive as a member, but also because his country had "strategic relevance" for Europe.

"The Mediterranean (region), especially the southern Mediterranean, has to be on the international agenda," De Marco told a news conference. "There will not be stability in Europe if there is not stability in the Mediterranean," he said.

Dini said he and De Marco discussed what strategy Malta should follow in regard to joining the EU, noting that Malta's application was "more advanced" than other countries in eastern Europe which also have asked to join the union.

Italy, when it held the EU's rotating presidency during the first six months of this year, had urged its partners to devote more attention to the Mediterranean area, saying the region's security depended on it.

Malta and Cyprus have undertakings from the EU that their membership applications will be considered six months after the 15-nation group completes a review, probably in mid-1997, on how to reform its workings and institutions.
